name: Alleged employment-access-to-disclosure-extortion sequence

attribution.legal_posture: Case-specific allegations in a federal indictment; they are pending allegations, with no adjudicated finding, ransomware characterization, or proof of destructive impact.

caveats: These episodes describe a demand; encryption and ransomware deployment are absent from the allegations.
The record describes reported conduct by specific fraudulent workers; theft, extortion, espionage, persistence, and sabotage remain case-specific.
Fraudulent employment, post-hire insider abuse, fake-interview malware, and external intrusion remain separate analytic tracks unless a source expressly establishes same-case overlap.
The indictment establishes charging posture; conviction and final merits ruling remain unresolved.

statements: The federal indictment describes three unnamed-employer episodes in which alleged workers obtained proprietary access through employment, demanded payment after termination or discovery, threatened public disclosure and then posted employer material. In one episode, the employer paid and the posted source code was removed; another allegedly caused substantial loss and damage.
limitations: No conviction or final merits ruling is established by the indictment.
Do not describe the demand as ransomware; no encryption or ransomware deployment is alleged in these episodes.
No people, personas, accounts, entities, victim organizations, raw data, sensitive selectors, images, wallets, payment identifiers, or private repository content are retained.
Fraudulent employment, post-hire insider abuse, fake-interview malware, and external intrusion remain separate analytic tracks unless a source expressly establishes same-case overlap.
Do not infer that every fraudulent worker performs theft, extortion, espionage, persistence, or sabotage.

sources.support: The indictment alleges that conspirators used employment access to obtain proprietary material, demanded additional payments after termination or discovery, threatened publication, and in three described episodes posted employer material on a public software-development website. One posting allegedly caused substantial loss and damage; in another episode, posted source code was removed after a payment.
